legal.title: Terms & Conditions
legal.description: Please read these terms and the refund policy before purchasing a course on Elemni.

refund.title: Refund & Cancellation Policy
refund.intro: You may request a cancellation or refund within 14 days of the purchase date. Requests are reviewed in line with the course access status and applicable law.

eligibility.title: Eligibility for Refund
items: You may request a refund within 14 days of your purchase date.
Submit your request through the Contact page or by calling the support number shown there.
We may ask for the transaction reference and the account used for the purchase.

nonRefundable.title: Non-Refundable Items
items: Requests submitted after 14 days, unless a longer right applies under law.
Digital content that has been substantially accessed may be excluded where permitted by law.
A refund cannot be issued for an amount that was never successfully charged.
Any mandatory consumer rights remain unaffected by this policy.

process.title: How to Request a Refund
steps: Open the Contact page and call the support number shown there.
Provide your transaction reference, account details, and reason for the request.
We will review the request and communicate the decision through the available contact details.
If approved, the refund is sent to the original payment method according to the payment provider's processing time.

sections.heading: 1. Acceptance of Terms
sections.content: By accessing and using Elemni (the "Platform"), you agree to be bound by these Terms & Conditions. If you do not agree, please do not use the Platform.

sections.heading: 2. User Registration
sections.content: You must provide accurate and complete information when creating an account. You are responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of your account credentials.

sections.heading: 3. Course Enrollment & Access
sections.content: Upon successful payment, you receive a non-transferable license to access the enrolled course content. Access is personal and cannot be shared or transferred.

sections.heading: 4. Payment & Pricing
sections.content: Prices are shown in Egyptian Pounds (EGP) at checkout. The amount confirmed by the payment provider is the amount charged for the transaction.

sections.heading: 5. Intellectual Property
sections.content: All course content, videos, materials, and the Platform itself are the intellectual property of Elemni and its instructors. Unauthorized reproduction or distribution is prohibited.

sections.heading: 6. User Conduct
sections.content: You agree not to: share account credentials, record or download course content, use the Platform for illegal purposes, or attempt to bypass security measures.

sections.heading: 7. Limitation of Liability
sections.content: Elemni shall not be liable for any indirect, incidental, or consequential damages. Our total liability shall not exceed the amount you paid for the course.

sections.heading: 8. Governing Law
sections.content: These Terms are interpreted under the applicable laws of the Arab Republic of Egypt. Mandatory consumer protections continue to apply.

landingQuizData.q1: In an AC circuit with an inductor of inductance (L) and a capacitor of capacitance (C), when is the circuit in resonance?
landingQuizData.q1o1: When inductive reactance equals capacitive reactance (XL = XC)
landingQuizData.q1o2: When the phase angle between voltage and current is 90 degrees
landingQuizData.q1o3: When resistance is at its highest
landingQuizData.q1o4: When no current flows through the circuit
landingQuizData.q1e: Resonance occurs in AC circuits when inductive reactance (XL) equals capacitive reactance (XC). The impedance (Z) is then at its minimum, equal to the resistance (R), and current is at its maximum.
landingQuizData.q2: What is the slope of the tangent to y = x³ - 3x at the point (2, 2)?
landingQuizData.q2e: The slope is the first derivative: y′ = 3x² - 3. At x = 2: y′ = 3(2)² - 3 = 12 - 3 = 9.
landingQuizData.q3: What is the grammatical role of the word “taliban” in a sentence meaning “Thirty students attended today”?
landingQuizData.q3o1: Direct object in the accusative case
landingQuizData.q3e: Arabic numbers from 11 to 99 take a singular accusative specification (tamyiz), so “taliban” is in the accusative case.
